Multi-negative cross entropy over a positive plus sampled negatives defines a candidate-ranking objective unless explicit catalog-normalization corrections are applied. Larger uniform pools increase compute and the chance of finding high-scoring negatives; distinguish mining-pool size M from retained-negative count K. For reproducible moderate-hard mining, specify score direction, quantile interval, sampling within that interval, random/hard proportions, replacement and deduplication. No universal optimal quantiles or curriculum emerge from the literature. Random warm-up followed by increasing hardness is a hypothesis to validate; adaptive-hardness research warns that fixed extreme hardness can select false negatives. [Adaptive hardness paper](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28709/29371)

Lower loss temperature concentrates gradients on high-scoring negatives, potentially amplifying both informative comparisons and label noise; distinguish it from the temperature used to sample negatives. Catalog-softmax approximation requires corrections based on actual sampling probabilities or expected counts, accounting for filtering, mixtures and selection. A uniform initial pool does not make mined negatives uniform; applying its log-probability after quantile selection is insufficient. Finite-sample corrected softmax also need not yield an unbiased loss. Uncorrected mixed-negative CE should therefore be described as a sampling-dependent ranking surrogate. [Candidate-sampling definitions](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf), [recommendation softmax analysis](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf)

Prefix-only exclusion leaves future positives and other relevant unobserved items eligible as negatives; always exclude the current target too. Hard mining can preferentially select these plausible positives. Random mixing, moderate hardness and gradual introduction are mitigation hypotheses, not guarantees. Do not inspect held-out labels to identify false negatives; compare settings using the fixed validation protocol. [Sequential false-negative research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116)
